explain.say: Here is a first-then board. First, the dentist. Then, the park. Knowing the fun bit is coming helps. A grown-up you trust can help you plan. Well done! Your challenge: practise opening wide and your stop hand.

steps.ask: What can help me feel calmer?

faq.a: You sit in a big chair that tips back. The dentist looks at your teeth with a small mirror and a light, and counts them. Usually it is quick.

faq.q: Can I ask the dentist to stop?
faq.a: Yes. Agree a signal first, like raising your hand. The dentist can pause for a moment.
asks: Tell me about Hand up to pause

faq.q: What can help me feel calmer?
faq.a: Bring a favourite toy, wear headphones, take slow breaths, or plan a fun then. A grown-up you trust can help.

faq.q: Why is the light so bright?
faq.a: The dentist needs a bright light to see inside your mouth. You can wear sunglasses if the bright light bothers you, if the dentist says yes.

faq.q: Is a doctor visit like this too?
faq.a: A bit. A doctor might listen to your chest or look in your ears. They tell you what they will do first. You can ask, What will happen next?

facts: Dentists use a small mirror to see the backs of your teeth.

quiz.say: You need a short pause at the dentist. What can you do?
quiz.show: You need a pause. What can you do?
quiz.why: Raising your hand is the agreed stop signal. The dentist pauses.

wrong.1: Biting could hurt the dentist. Use your hand signal.
wrong.2: Running is unsafe. Your hand signal works.

quiz.say: How does the dentist want Hana to feel?
quiz.show: How does the dentist want Hana to feel?
quiz.why: The dentist is gentle and explains things, so Hana feels safe.

wrong.1: The dentist wants to help, not scare.
wrong.2: The dentist wants Hana to feel okay.
